rv.q: This production has none of the broadness or festive spirit of a Christmas show or panto, but the wonder and magic of both.
That sophistication is matched by nuanced, vocally commanding performances in the ensemble, whether from Chumisa Dornford

Jordan Fein’s revival of Stephen Sondheim and James Lapine’s musical mash-up of the Brothers’ fairy tales is an absolute hoot - gorgeously dressed and designed by Tom Scutt and bottling all their stories’ subversive enchantment.
This production is very Fein indeed.
But this is also a transporting wonder – everything you could wish for and more.
There isn’t a weak link among them as strong-voiced and subtle they bring fictive characters to grounded life.
This musical has an unmistakably elegant froideur about it, making it easier to admire than love.
For anyone yet to experience this iconic musical, this production honours the heart of Into the Woods while offering a subtle, cohesive and wholly absorbing version.
Nevertheless, if you haven’t seen it, if you go down to Into The Woods tonight, you’re sure of a big surprise.
